title: Push Security warns of phishing emails with fake seminar and expert-interview invitations in the names of Nvidia, Coca-Cola and others
date_note: ITHome's page gives only its publication day, 27 November 2026; the page gives no earlier date for Push Security's warning.
summary: ITHome reports that security firm Push Security warned of phishing emails faking invitations to online seminars or paid expert interviews. The impersonated companies named are Accenture, Coca-Cola, Culver's, Google Cloud, Spotify, Nvidia and SpaceX. Links are sent through legitimate services (SendGrid, Cvent, Mandrill, HireVue) to a fake Google sign-in page. Researchers suspect AI coding assistants were used to build the kits.
plain: Push Security warns of fake invitation emails, using well-known company names, that lead to a fake Google sign-in page meant to capture logins.
exec: Fake invitations that come through legitimate email services can make credential-theft phishing harder to spot.
action: ITHome's report advises avoiding clicking links in such invitations and verifying that the invitation is genuine.
geo_basis: no victim or location stated on the page read; global warning

validation.note: Only ITHome China was read; Push Security's own post was not found, so the findings are as relayed by ITHome.
